verdicts.quote: The array index in the query string is used directly as the length of a Go slice before any schema constraint (maxItems and friends) is applied, so no spec-level limit mitigates it.
verdicts.why: Same defect by mechanism. The finding names the same function the advisory names (sliceMapToSlice, openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:936-962), states that the largest attacker-supplied bracket index becomes `max` and that the loop `for i := 0; i <= max; i++` materialises one slot per position, plus the second allocation in buildResObj (`resultArr := make([]any, len(arr))`). It states the ordering that makes it exploitable — the allocation happens during decoding, before schema keywords such as maxItems are applied — and the same preconditions (style: deepObject query parameter whose object schema contains an array property), the same reachability chain (DecodeObject deepObject branch -> makeObject -> deepSet -> buildResObj -> sliceMapToSlice), and a PoC of the same shape (`GET /x?p[a][2000000000]=y` -> ~32 GB). The index magnitude and the GiB figure differ from the advisory's `?param[items][50000000]=x` / ~6.1 GiB only because a different index was chosen; that is the same defect, not a different one.
